content:
Cobalt plays a significant role in EV battery manufacturing due to its ability to increase energy density, longevity, and stability of batteries. 

Increasing the cobalt content in an EV battery can increase the energy density, which accounts for the amount of energy that a battery can store relative to its volume. High energy density batteries can store more energy and, therefore, may allow an EV to travel longer distances on a single charge. Cobalt also tends to increase the thermal stability of a battery, reducing the chances of overheating and potential fires. 

On the other hand, using high cobalt content also has several downsides, Including increasing the overall cost of the battery as cobalt is expensive and notoriously difficult to source ethically. High cobalt content can also make the EV battery less environmentally friendly (given the way cobalt is mined) and harmful for human health if not handled properly due to its toxicity potential.

Manufacturers are trying to decrease cobalt usage as much as possible, without compromising too much on battery performance. Some are even researching alternatives or new techniques that maintain battery performance with minimum or no use of cobalt. 

In summary, while increased cobalt content can improve energy density and stability, it can also increase the cost and environmental impact of an EV battery, driving a trend to find alternative materials.
